lines.en: label nodokaspecial30p2:
scene noonsky
: So, how far away is this book store thingy?
lines.zh: : 那么，那个什么书店还有多远？

lines.en: : Wait...your signing {i}is{/i} at a book store, right? Because I have a library book I’ve been holding onto for five years now and I get nervous any time I have to go inside one.
lines.zh: : 等等……你的签售{i}是{/i}在书店办吧？因为我有一本图书馆的书已经借了五年没还，每次不得不走进那种地方，我都会紧张。

lines.en: : They’re onto me. I know they are.
lines.zh: : 他们盯上我了。我知道的。

lines.en: : Does...Futaba know about this?
lines.zh: : 那个……Futaba 知道这事吗？

lines.en: : No. And she never will, so keep your mouth closed.
lines.zh: : 不。而且她永远都不会知道，所以你给我把嘴闭上。

lines.en: : Hmm...I believe the venue is about a quarter mile away. But if it’s alright with you, I’d like to make another quick detour for more coffee.
lines.zh: : 嗯……场地大概在四分之一英里外吧。不过如果诸位不介意，我想再绕一小段路去买咖啡。

lines.en: : You are literally holding a cup of coffee right now.
lines.zh: : 你现在手里就端着一杯咖啡。

lines.en: : That I am. And if my calculations are correct, which they always are, I’ll be finished with that coffee by the time we arrive at the next shop.
lines.zh: : 正是。而如果我的计算没错——而它们从来没错——等我们走到下一家店时，这杯就见底了。

lines.en: : You have an addiction and you need help.
lines.zh: : 你这是成瘾了，需要治疗。

lines.en: : As do you and no one ever tries to rehabilitate {i}you.{/i}
lines.zh: : 您也一样，可从来没人想着把{i}您{/i}戒掉。

lines.en: : That’s because Sensei’s addiction keeps a bunch of girls from going crazy and rubbing up against stuff. Yours just keeps you awake.
lines.zh: : 那是因为 Sensei 的瘾能让一堆女生不至于发疯去蹭东西。你的瘾只能让你保持清醒。

lines.en: : Ew. To the girls part. Not the awake part.
lines.zh: : 呕。是恶心“女生”那部分。“清醒”那部分不恶心。

lines.en: : I’m a girl. You’re a girl. Nodoka’s probably a girl. Are you saying we’re all gross as well?
lines.zh: : 我是女生。你是女生。Nodoka 大概也算女生。你是说我们也都恶心咯？

lines.en: : I’m saying I don’t want to have a casual conversation about our teacher’s sex addiction. Are we getting coffee or not?
lines.zh: : 我是说，我不想这么随随便便地聊我们老师的性瘾。到底还去不去买咖啡？

lines.en: : We are. But I must first take another detour to {i}rub up against stuff{/i} as Sensei’s sickness hasn’t spread to me yet and I’m beginning to get a little crazy.
lines.zh: : 去。不过我得先再绕段路去{i}蹭点东西{/i}，因为 Sensei 的病还没传染给我，而我已经开始有点发疯了。

lines.en: : Beginning? You’re already batshit insane. Sensei, I don’t want to take another detour. Can you just, infect Nodoka really quick or something? Thanks.
lines.zh: : 开始？你早就疯得没救了。Sensei，我不想再绕路了。您能不能干脆点，赶紧把 Nodoka 传染一下什么的？谢了。

lines.en: : No thanks. I’m sure I {i}could,{/i} but I’m afraid of what I’d catch from her.
lines.zh: : 不，谢了。我确信我{i}能做到{/i}，但我怕从她身上染上什么。

lines.en: : You’d catch nothing but a good time. Come to me, Father. Infect me with your desire. Make me {i}sick.{/i}
lines.zh: : 您染上的只会是段美好时光。来我这儿吧，父亲。用您的欲望感染我。让我{i}生病{/i}。

lines.en: : Pretty sure the only one getting sick here is me...
lines.zh: : 我敢肯定，这里唯一要吐的人是我……

lines.en: scene black

No one becomes infected, but Nodoka does manage to obtain another cup of liquid courage that she carries along with her to the venue (Which, luckily for Rin, is {i}not{/i} a library but a very large bookstore.)
lines.zh: 没有人被传染，倒是 Nodoka 成功又弄到了一杯“液体勇气”，一路端着走向会场（对 Rin 来说幸运的是，那{i}不是{/i}图书馆，而是一家很大的书店。）

lines.en: Upon entering, I’m shocked to see just how many people turned up. And, while I’d love to be able to tell you that many of them are just here to shop...that doesn’t seem like the case.
lines.zh: 一进门，我就被到场的人数惊到了。虽然我很想告诉你们，其中很多人只是来买书的……但看起来并非如此。

lines.en: Nodoka is recognized immediately and pulled away from our group so that she can get set-up at a table on the second floor of the shop, leaving the rest of us to awkwardly look around for something to do.
lines.zh: Nodoka 立刻被人认出来，从我们这群人里被拉走，去二楼的一张桌子后做准备，留下我们几个尴尬地四处张望，想找点事做。

lines.en: Carefully and slowly, we make our way through the crowd and manage to scope out a small space of unoccupied standing room that we quickly claim as our own.
lines.zh: 我们小心翼翼地在人群里挪动，终于找到一小块没人占的落脚地，赶紧据为己有。

lines.en: Thanks to my height, I’m able to see over the crowd, but the same can’t be said for Rin and Otoha who struggle to stare between the gaps in onlookers.
lines.zh: 多亏我个子高，能越过人群看过去；Rin 和 Otoha 就不行了，只能从围观者的缝隙里费力地张望。

lines.en: There’s something bothering me, though.
lines.zh: 不过有件事让我在意。

lines.en: I can’t seem to go five seconds without someone looking at me and whispering to their friends or partner about something.
lines.zh: 每隔不到五秒，就有人看着我，跟朋友或同伴低声说些什么。

lines.en: Rin and Otoha catch onto this well, but don’t appear to understand why either.
lines.zh: Rin 和 Otoha 也察觉到了，但显然也不明白为什么。

lines.en: It makes me very uncomfortable.
lines.zh: 这让我非常不自在。

lines.en: I never fit in anywhere to begin with, but drowning in this sea of inaudible gossip is starting to drive me-
lines.zh: 我本来就不属于任何地方，可淹没在这片听不清内容的闲言碎语之海里，开始把我逼得——

lines.en: : Attention, please. Today’s Q&A panel is about to begin.
lines.zh: : 请注意。今天的问答环节即将开始。

lines.en: : Please keep all questions brief and do not interrupt one another while someone is speaking.
lines.zh: : 请各位提问时尽量简短，他人发言时请勿打断。

lines.en: : We understand just how many of you are passionate about the first installment of this new series, but we urge you to remain calm and collected as Miss Nagahara speaks.
lines.zh: : 我们非常理解各位对本系列第一部热情高涨，但在 Nagahara 小姐讲话期间，请务必保持冷静与克制。

lines.en: : Repeat offenders will be escorted out of the venue and banned from attending any future events both related to and {i}unrelated{/i} to today’s author.
lines.zh: : 屡犯者将被请离会场，并被禁止参加今后任何与今日作者相关或{i}不相关{/i}的活动。

lines.en: : With that said, on behalf of the Kumon-mi Literary Committee, I’d like to thank today's guest for appearing and urge all of you to provide a very warm welcome...to S.A. Nagahara!
lines.zh: : 那么，我谨代表 Kumon-mi 文学委员会，感谢今日嘉宾的到场，并请各位以最热烈的掌声欢迎……S.A. Nagahara！

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign1
The crowd erupts into a fit of applause as Nodoka- or, excuse me, {i}S.A. Nagahara{/i} takes her seat at a table stacked with copies of what I can only imagine is her latest book.
lines.zh: 人群爆发出一阵掌声，Nodoka——啊，抱歉，{i}S.A. Nagahara{/i}——在她那张堆满了书的桌子后面坐下，那些书我想就是她的新作。

lines.en: Her composure and refusal to stop the crowd from applauding signals to me that she’s done this before, and I’m surprised to see just how well-established she is for her age.
lines.zh: 她泰然自若，也不急着让大家停止鼓掌，这让我看出她以前干过这事儿。以她的年纪能有这样的地位，我有些意外。

lines.en: Though, if she’s going to lie about her name, I’m sure that most of the people in this crowd are unaware of how old she really is in the first place.
lines.zh: 不过，既然她连名字都要撒谎，我敢肯定在场的大多数人本来就不清楚她的真实年龄。

lines.en: The applause slowly dies down and, as it does, Nodoka’s eyes open.
lines.zh: 掌声渐渐平息，与此同时，Nodoka 睁开了眼睛。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign2
: Wooooow...quite the turn-out we have today, isn’t it?
lines.zh: : 哇哦哦哦……今天到场的人可真不少，不是吗？

lines.en: : I suppose trying something a little different was worth it after all.
lines.zh: : 看来尝试一点不一样的东西，终究还是值得的。

lines.en: : You flatter me. You really do.
lines.zh: : 你们太抬举我了。真的。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign3
: Now, let’s see...
lines.zh: : 那么，让我想想……

lines.en: : Normally, this is the part where I’d give a brief synopsis of the book. Maybe a little background information about how it came to be or {i}why{/i} it came to be, but...
lines.zh: : 通常到了这里，我会简短地介绍一下本书的内容梗概。也许再讲点背景——它是怎么来的、{i}为什么{/i}来的，不过……

lines.en: : Frankly, I don’t see why that would be necessary given that you’re already {i}here,{/i} aren’t you?
lines.zh: : 坦白说，既然你们都已经{i}来了{/i}，我不认为还有这个必要，不是吗？

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign4
: You would not {i}be{/i} here if you didn’t already know what this book was about.
lines.zh: : 如果你们不知道这本书讲什么，就不会站{i}在这里{/i}了。

lines.en: : You would not {i}be{/i} here if you weren’t already curious about the characters or the story...or what will come next.
lines.zh: : 如果你们不对角色、对故事……或者对接下来会发生什么感到好奇，也不会站{i}在这里{/i}了。

lines.en: : And so, perhaps it would be in everyone’s best interests if we skipped right over the formalities and just opened the floor.
lines.zh: : 所以，也许对大家都好的是，我们干脆跳过这些繁文缛节，直接开放提问。

lines.en: : What do you say?
lines.zh: : 你们说呢？

lines.en: The crowd erupts again and, while it’s certainly loud and obnoxious, it takes some of the focus off of me.
lines.zh: 人群再次沸腾。虽然确实吵得要命，但多少把一部分注意力从我身上挪开了。

lines.en: And I’m thankful for that.
lines.zh: 对此我心怀感激。

lines.en: : Go on. Raise your hands. You know how this works.
lines.zh: : 来吧，举起手。你们知道规矩的。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign5
The hands go up and the volume goes down.
lines.zh: 手举了起来，音量降了下去。

lines.en: Then, almost mechanically, Nodoka begins moving through the audience one by one.
lines.zh: 接着，Nodoka 近乎机械地开始一个接一个地扫过观众席。

lines.en: : Hmm...you. In the shirt. What would you like to know?
lines.zh: : 嗯……你。穿那件衬衫的。你想知道什么？

lines.en: : Well, first off, I’d like to thank you for deviating from your typical formula and branching out into something far surpassing what the typical reader would call “taboo.”
lines.zh: : 首先，我想感谢您跳脱出惯常的套路，涉足了远远超出普通读者所谓“禁忌”的领域。

lines.en: : Which is saying a lot for an author who hasn’t shied away from including sex scenes containing literal farm animals.
lines.zh: : 对一个从不回避写性爱场面、甚至写过货真价实的农场动物的作者来说，这评价可不低。

lines.en: : We all know what really happens on farms. I’m not one to shy away from the truth. But what is the question?
lines.zh: : 农场里到底会发生什么，大家心里都有数。我可不是会回避真相的人。不过你的问题是？

lines.en: : The question is...why a school?
lines.zh: : 我的问题是……为什么是学校？

lines.en: : There are so many other books and media series focusing on schools and, up until now, you’ve always seemed to challenge standard conventions and cliches.
lines.zh: : 已经有那么多书和影视作品把舞台放在学校了，而在此之前，您一直都在挑战那些标准套路和陈词滥调。

lines.en: : Are you calling my latest work cliche?
lines.zh: : 你是在说我的新作很老套？

lines.en: : Not at all! I-
lines.zh: : 完全没有！我——

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign6
: I’m kidding. There’s no need to get flustered. It’s a good question.
lines.zh: : 开玩笑的。没必要慌。这是个好问题。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign7
: I suppose the easiest answer would be...that a school simply is the perfect setting to facilitate the type of story I wanted to tell and the themes I wanted to explore.
lines.zh: : 我想，最简单的答案是……学校恰恰是最完美的舞台，能承载我想讲的那种故事、我想探讨的那些主题。

lines.en: : Anyone could mimic Nabokov. There are more “Lolita” clones than one can count — and it was not my goal to follow the same steps that many before me have tripped over.
lines.zh: : 谁都能模仿纳博科夫。“洛丽塔”的仿品多得数不清——而我的目标可不是踩着前人摔过的脚印往前走。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign8
: But when you want to create an entire well of debauchery — a haven for misdeeds even, there is no better place to look than where the innocent gather most.
lines.zh: : 但当你想挖出一整口堕落之井——甚至一座为恶行准备的避难所时，没有比天真之人最密集的地方更合适的了。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign9
: Next question...You. In the other shirt.
lines.zh: : 下一个问题……你。穿另一件衬衫的。

lines.en: : Th-Thank you! Huge fan! I’ve been following you since “Every Day I Grow Some More!”
lines.zh: : 谢、谢谢！超级粉丝！我从《每天都在长大一点！》就开始追您了！

lines.en: : Aww, you flatter me. What’s your question?
lines.zh: : 哎呀，太抬举我了。你的问题是？

lines.en: : M-My question is...how confident are you in ending a series with so many prospective love interests?!
lines.zh: : 我、我的问题是……您对让一个系列带着这么多可能的恋爱对象收尾，有多大把握？！

lines.en: : Up...Up until now, you’ve always cited “Why choose?” as a lazy, uninspired book trope! Have...Have you changed your opinion?!
lines.zh: : 到、在此之前，您一直把“为什么要选一个？”称作懒惰又毫无灵气的书套路！难、难道您改变看法了吗？！

lines.en: : I have not. And, to be quite honest, I’m not too concerned with how the story will end at this point in time.
lines.zh: : 没有。而且说实话，眼下我并不怎么在意故事会如何收场。

lines.en: : What we have in “The Light of Last Summer” is not a run of the mill romance. In fact, I struggle to call it {i}romance{/i} at all.
lines.zh: : 《去年夏日之光》不是一个普通的恋爱故事。事实上，我很难把它称作{i}恋爱故事{/i}。

lines.en: : It’s an in-depth character study of a large group of flawed and misguided individuals who, for the most part, do not {i}deserve{/i} love.
lines.zh: : 它是一份深入的角色研究，研究一大群有缺陷、误入歧途的个体——他们中的大多数，都{i}不配{/i}得到爱。

lines.en: : I’m sure you’d all agree that I am {i}very{/i} good at what I do. But there is no conceivable way for {i}any{/i} author to believably end a series with {i}this{/i} many pairings in a way that is good for all of them.
lines.zh: : 我相信你们都会同意，我{i}很{/i}擅长我做的事情。但{i}任何{/i}作家都不可能让一个系列带着{i}这么多{/i}配对，还能以一种对所有人都不错的方式收尾。

lines.en: : Some of the students will have to suffer for others to prosper. And in the prospering of those others, the sorrow in the background is sure to leak into everything else.
lines.zh: : 有些学生必须受苦，另一些才能得救。而在后者得救的同时，背景里的悲哀必然会渗进其他一切。

lines.en: : No one can win, and I believe that is evident even this early on in the series.
lines.zh: : 没有人能赢，我相信即便在系列这么早的阶段，这一点也已经很明显了。

lines.en: : Is it just me or...does Nodoka’s new book sound a lot like...
lines.zh: : 是我的错觉吗……Nodoka 的新书听起来很像……

lines.en: : It’s not just you.
lines.zh: : 不只是你的错觉。

lines.en: : That’s exactly what it is.
lines.zh: : 就是那么回事。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign10
: You. In the third shirt. Question?
lines.zh: : 你。穿第三件衬衫的。有问题？

lines.en: : Yes! Hi! Uhh...let’s see...
lines.zh: : 有！您好！呃……让我想想……

lines.en: : I actually have two questions.
lines.zh: : 我其实有两个问题。

lines.en: : No you don’t. Pick one.
lines.zh: : 不，你没有。选一个。

lines.en: : Just one? Uhh...okay...umm...
lines.zh: : 就一个？呃……好吧……嗯……

lines.en: : Is there a reason the main character seems so...closed off? He’s written well, but without any background information {i}at all{/i} in the first book, he seems like more of an...afterthought than anything?
lines.zh: : 为什么主角看起来那么……封闭？他写得很好，可第一本书里{i}一点{/i}背景信息都没有，他看起来更像是个……事后才补上的角色？

lines.en: : Does he? Because {i}I{/i} think he’s plenty interesting even without any of that.
lines.zh: : 是吗？可{i}我{/i}觉得即便没有那些，他也够有意思了。

lines.en: : It takes a very special type of person to groom and manipulate an entire class of underage girls. It takes someone {i}sick.{/i} And most people catch their sicknesses from someone else.
lines.zh: : 要去调教和操纵一整班的未成年少女，需要一种非常特殊的人。需要某个{i}病态{/i}的人。而大多数人的病，都是从别人那儿染来的。

lines.en: : Are you saying...the protagonist is only like this because someone else corrupted him?
lines.zh: : 您是说……主角之所以是这副样子，是因为有别人把他带坏了？

lines.en: : I’m saying you should spend more time thinking about the implications of a character’s actions rather than their motivations for doing so. Unless you want to be bored, that is.
lines.zh: : 我是说，你该多花点心思去想一个角色的行为所蕴含的意味，而不是他们做事的动机。除非你想觉得无聊，那是另说。

lines.en: : Any wannabe-psychologist could sit down with a pen and paper and try to tell you about {i}why{/i} people act the way they do.
lines.zh: : 随便哪个半吊子心理学家都能拿着纸笔坐下来，试图告诉你人{i}为什么{/i}会那样行事。

lines.en: : But with so many of our decisions not based in science or logic but a spontaneous impulse or thought, what matter does motivation carry? If you ask me, none.
lines.zh: : 可既然我们那么多的决定并不是基于科学或逻辑，而是出于一时的冲动或念头，动机又有什么要紧？要我说，一点也不要紧。

lines.en: : It matters not {i}why{/i} someone does the things they do. What matters is what spawns from that. And to me, it’s far more fun to predict the future than to analyze the past.
lines.zh: : 一个人{i}为什么{/i}做那些事并不重要。重要的是从中生出了什么。而对我来说，预测未来远比分析过去有趣。

lines.en: : T-Thank you, Miss Nagahara! But if you wouldn’t mind-
lines.zh: : 谢、谢谢您，Nagahara 小姐！不过如果您不介意的话——

lines.en: : Fine, fine. What’s your next question?
lines.zh: : 行行行。你的下一个问题是什么？

lines.en: : There’s, umm...
lines.zh: : 那个，嗯……

lines.en: : There’s a lot less...{i}girl on girl{/i} action in your new book. I just wanted to know if-
lines.zh: : 您的新书里……{i}女生和女生{/i}之间的戏份少了很多。我只是想知道——

lines.en: : It’s coming. Don’t worry.
lines.zh: : 会有的。别担心。

lines.en: : And it’ll be sooner than you think.
lines.zh: : 而且会比你想象的来得更快。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign11
: Thank you so much! I’m looking forward to reading it!
lines.zh: : 太感谢您了！我已经迫不及待想看了！

lines.en: : Not as much as I’m looking forward to {i}writing{/i} it.
lines.zh: : 我迫不及待想{i}写{/i}的程度，可比你深。

lines.en: : Heheh...heh...
: You know, this is what we get for not reading her book. We could have avoided this.
lines.zh: : 知道吗，这就是我们没读她那本书的报应。我们本来可以避免这一切的。

lines.en: : Heh...heheh...
: You. In the shirt without sleeves.
lines.zh: : 你。穿无袖衬衫的。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign12
: Aren’t you the girl who hit on me at the bar on Halloween?
lines.zh: : 你不是万圣节那天在酒吧搭讪我的那个女孩吗？

lines.en: : Hmm...did I do something like that? That doesn’t sound like me. I’m very reclusive.
lines.zh: : 嗯……我做过那种事吗？听起来不像我。我很宅的。

lines.en: : No, I’m pretty sure it was you. Also, aren’t you in high school? I’m pretty positive I’ve seen you around the dorms.
lines.zh: : 不，我很确定就是你。还有，你不是还在上高中吗？我相当肯定在宿舍那边见过你。

lines.en: : Aren’t you a grown woman? What are you doing hanging out in high school dorms?
lines.zh: : 你不也是个成年女人吗？你跑到高中宿舍里晃悠什么？

lines.en: : Oh my God! It’s just like the book!
lines.zh: : 我的天！简直跟书里一模一样！

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign13
: Hey, it’s not that weird! I live there! Of course I’m going to see some girls hanging around!
lines.zh: : 喂，这有什么好奇怪的！我就住在那儿！当然会看到几个女生在附近晃！

lines.en: : Talk about being a fanatic. This woman’s literally trying to become the main character of the book. She’s missing the point entirely.
lines.zh: : 这才叫狂热粉丝吧。这女人简直是在努力变成书里的主角。她完全没抓到重点。

lines.en: : I don’t even know this book! I just saw a line and got into it! I do that sometimes!
lines.zh: : 我连这本书是什么都不知道！我就是看见排了条长队才跟进去的！我有时候就是会这样！

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign14
: Why is my mom here?! I barely saw her at all these last couple years and now it’s like I can’t even get away!
lines.zh: : 我妈为什么在这儿？！这几年我几乎没怎么见过她，现在倒好，我想躲都躲不开！

lines.en: : On the bright side...at least she’s not reading Nodoka’s books?
lines.zh: : 往好处想……至少她没在读 Nodoka 的书？

lines.en: : Mom! Go home!
lines.zh: : 妈！回家去！

lines.en: : Rin! Hey, Rin! Tell everyone how it’s not weird for me to live in the dorms with you!
lines.zh: : Rin！嘿，Rin！你跟大家说说，我跟你一起住在宿舍里一点都不奇怪！

lines.en: : It totally {i}is{/i} weird! You should leave! I want my life back!
lines.zh: : 奇怪{i}死了{/i}！你该走了！把我的生活还给我！

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign15
: Hey, wait...is that group cosplaying?
lines.zh: : 等等，那几个人是在角色扮演吗？

lines.en: : Oh my God! I think they are! That’s almost exactly how I pictured Sensei in the book!
lines.zh: : 我的天！我觉得是！那几乎就是我在书里想象的 Sensei 的样子！

lines.en: : We have to take his pants off to know for sure...I look kind of like Haruhi, don’t I? Do you think he’ll do it with me? I can pretend I have a husband and everything.
lines.zh: : 我们得把他的裤子脱下来才能确定……我长得是不是有点像 Haruhi？你觉得他会跟我做吗？我可以假装自己有老公什么的。

lines.en: : Oh! And those girls with him must be Ren and Otoka! Do you think they’re his daughters?
lines.zh: : 哇！那跟他一起的女孩肯定是 Ren 和 Otoka！你们觉得是他女儿吗？

lines.en: : I don’t know, but I suddenly want them to kiss!
lines.zh: : 不知道，但我突然好想看她们接吻！

lines.en: : Kiss! Kiss! Kiss! Kiss! Kiss! Kiss!
lines.zh: : 亲一个！亲一个！亲一个！亲一个！亲一个！亲一个！

lines.en: : I had a feeling something like this might happen...
lines.zh: : 我就有种预感会发生这种事……

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign16
: Now, now. Settle down, everyone. Leave the {i}cosplayers{/i} alone.
lines.zh: : 好了好了。各位安静。别去打扰那几位{i}角色扮演{/i}的。

lines.en: : I’m sure there are plenty more questions that need to be answered and I don’t have all day...
lines.zh: : 我敢肯定还有很多问题等着回答，而我可没一整天的时间……

lines.en: scene black
The Q&A carries on, getting more and more disturbing with each and every question.
lines.zh: 问答继续进行，每一个问题都比上一个更让人不适。

lines.en: This isn’t just a book.
lines.zh: 这不只是一本书。

lines.en: This is {i}us.{/i}
lines.zh: 这就是{i}我们{/i}。

lines.en: This is {i}our{/i} story.
lines.zh: 这就是{i}我们{/i}的故事。

lines.en: And she’s putting the entire thing on display for everyone...
lines.zh: 而她正把这一切摊开，展示给所有人……

lines.en: She’s showing them all who I really am...
lines.zh: 她在向他们展示真正的我是谁……

lines.en: She’s showing them everything...
lines.zh: 她在向他们展示一切……

lines.en: And...
And they...
lines.zh: 而他们……

lines.en: And they {i}like{/i} me...
lines.zh: 而他们{i}喜欢{/i}我……

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign17
: Hey! Bar buddy! Long time, no see. Didn’t realize you read this kind of stuff. That’s not weird or anything. I’m not judging you.
lines.zh: : 嘿！酒吧的伙伴！好久不见。没想到你会看这种东西。这一点都不奇怪什么的。我没有在评判你。

lines.en: : I don’t read {i}this kind of stuff,{/i} Rika. That girl is one of my students.
lines.zh: : 我不看{i}这种东西{/i}，Rika。那个女孩是我的学生。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign18
: Okay. That’s a relief because I was totally judging you.
lines.zh: : 行吧。那我就放心了，因为我刚才可是在狠狠地评判你。

lines.en: : Haven’t you jerked someone off under the bleachers before? Why are {i}you{/i} judging {i}me?{/i}
lines.zh: : {i}你{/i}以前不还在看台底下给人打过飞机吗？凭什么评判{i}我{/i}？

lines.en: : Dude, that was the 90’s. If you weren’t jerking someone off under the bleachers, what were you even doing?
lines.zh: : 老兄，那可是九十年代。要是你没在看台底下给人打飞机，那你到底在干嘛？

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign19
: Also, that’s not even the part I was judging you for. I got laid watching Cannibal Holocaust once. Disturbing content or whatever doesn’t bother me. But super smart people like that?
lines.zh: : 再说，我要评判的也不是那个。我有一次一边看《食人族大屠杀》一边做爱。那种什么猎奇内容吓不到我。可像她那种聪明绝顶的人呢？

lines.en: : That stuff creeps me the fuck out. That girl’s, like...the head of a cult already. And I’m not looking to get sucked into another one of those things.
lines.zh: : 那种东西把老子吓得够呛。那女孩简直……已经是个邪教教主了。我可不想再被卷进那种东西里去。

lines.en: : Knew there had to be an ulterior motive for her hitting on me. No one wants a single 42 year-old woman covered in tattoos.
lines.zh: : 我就知道她当初搭讪我必有别的企图。没人会想要一个满身纹身的 42 岁单身女人。

lines.en: : You’re 43! Stop lying to everyone!
lines.zh: : 你明明 43 了！别再对所有人撒谎了！

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign20
: No, {i}you{/i} stop lying to everyone! I’m going through enough!
lines.zh: : {i}你{/i}才别对所有人撒谎！我已经够难受了！

lines.en: : Are you really still in the dorms? It’s been months.
lines.zh: : 你真还住在宿舍里？都好几个月了。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign21
: Like I said, I’m going through enough. But things might take a turn for the better soon. We’ll see.
lines.zh: : 说了，我已经够难受了。不过事情可能很快就会好转。走着瞧吧。

lines.en: : You got anything planned for the rest of the day? I was gonna go grab dinner if you wanted to tag along.
lines.zh: : 你今天接下来有什么安排？我打算去吃个晚饭，你要不要一起？

lines.en: : I have plans with a cult leader already, but maybe next time.
lines.zh: : 我已经跟一位邪教教主有约了，下次吧。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign22

: Suit yourself. You might want to be careful around that girl, though. She denied it, but I totally know she was the one who hit on me. You might be next. Some girls are just into age gaps like that.
lines.zh: : 随你。不过你最好小心点那个女孩。她否认了，但我百分百确定当初搭讪我的就是她。下一个说不定就是你。有些女生就是好这口年龄差。

lines.en: : I will remain vigilant and oppose any and all sexual contact with her.
lines.zh: : 我会保持警惕，抵制与她发生任何性接触。

lines.en: : Cool, cool. Cool.
lines.zh: : 行，行。行。

lines.en: : I’m gonna give you my phone number.
lines.zh: : 我要把我的电话号码给你。

lines.en: : You are?
lines.zh: : 你要给我？

lines.en: : Yeah. I tried to think of a cool lead-in to that or a way to sound smooth or whatever, but I couldn’t come up with anything. So I’m just gonna give it to you.
lines.zh: : 对。我本来想找个酷一点的开头，或者说得顺溜一点什么的，可想不出来。所以我就直接给你了。

lines.en: : Are you hitting on me right now? Your daughter is like ten feet away.
lines.zh: : 你这是在搭讪我吗？你女儿就在十英尺外。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign23
: I’m not hitting on you. I just desperately need friends to distract me from the darkness that is consuming all that I am and Rin keeps telling me I’m 43 and making things even darker.
lines.zh: : 我没在搭讪你。我只是非常需要朋友来分散注意力，好不去想那团正在吞噬我整个人的黑暗，而 Rin 一直提醒我 43 岁，把事情弄得更黑暗了。

lines.en: : Are you {i}sure{/i} you’re not hitting on me? Because you can be and I won’t mind.
lines.zh: : 你{i}确定{/i}你不是在搭讪我吗？因为你可以搭讪，我不会介意的。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign24
: Aren’t you dating Imani?
lines.zh: : 你不是在跟 Imani 交往吗？

lines.en: : Imani? No. We just work together. Same with Wakana. And I’m pretty sure we told you that.
lines.zh: : Imani？没有。我们只是同事。Wakana 也是。而且我敢肯定我们跟你说过。

lines.en: : Yeah, but my ex told me she loved me and that was clearly a lie, so.
lines.zh: : 是啊，可我前任也跟我说过她爱我，那显然是谎话，所以。

lines.en: : I’m not dating Imani. And if I was, I probably would have said something about it when the two of you made out.
lines.zh: : 我没在跟 Imani 交往。而且就算我在交往，你们俩接吻那会儿我大概早就提过了。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign25
: Ohhhhh...yeah. She was so average that I guess I forgot about it already.
lines.zh: : 哦哦哦……对。她太平庸了，我大概已经忘了。

lines.en: Oh, poor Imani...
lines.zh: 哦，可怜的 Imani……

lines.en: I can’t wait to tease her more about this.
lines.zh: 我已经等不及要拿这事多逗逗她了。

lines.en: scene nodokabooksign26
: Anyway, I’m gonna head out. But you should call me sometime when you’re not busy joining a cult.
lines.zh: : 总之，我走了。不过你不忙着加入邪教的时候，可以给我打个电话。

lines.en: : Also, if they try to brand you, don’t let them. It hurts when it happens and then it hurts again when you have to tattoo over it.
lines.zh: : 还有，如果他们想给你烙印，别让他们烙。烙的时候疼，之后还得纹身盖住，又疼一次。

lines.en: : Later.
lines.zh: : 回见。

lines.en: scene black
$ rikanumber = True
Rika heads out and I return to Rin and Otoha just before our semi-famous author friend rejoins the fray.
lines.zh: Rika 离开，我回到 Rin 和 Otoha 身边，紧接着我们那位半著名的作家朋友也重新加入了战局。

lines.en: Not wanting the crowd to swarm her, the four of us take shelter in the store’s employee lounge for an hour or two as Rin and Otoha give Nodoka a stern lecture on the value of privacy.
lines.zh: 为了不让人群围堵她，我们四个躲进书店的员工休息室待了一两个小时，期间 Rin 和 Otoha 对 Nodoka 进行了一顿关于隐私价值的严厉说教。

lines.en: I elect to not chime in, despite being perhaps the most violated out of everyone, but it’s not because I’m not upset with her.
lines.zh: 我没有插嘴，尽管我大概是所有人里被侵犯得最厉害的那个——但这不代表我不生她的气。

lines.en: In fact, she was {i}right{/i} earlier when she said this was something I’d want to see.
lines.zh: 事实上，她先前说得{i}对{/i}，这正是我想看的东西。

lines.en: I {i}am{/i} proud of her — but it’s for all the wrong reasons.
lines.zh: 我为她骄傲——却{i}是{/i}出于各种错误的理由。

lines.en: And, disturbed as I may be, I can’t help but feel shocked about how closely she’s watched me.
lines.zh: 而且，尽管我很不安，我还是忍不住震惊于她对我观察得有多细致。

lines.en: And just how well she seems to understand.
lines.zh: 以及她理解得有多透彻。

lines.en: My curiosity grows stronger, causing several uncertain uncertainties to dissipate.
lines.zh: 我的好奇心愈发强烈，好几个不确定的未知也随之消散。

lines.en: All the while, she continues to hollow out a segment of my heart to live in.
lines.zh: 与此同时，她继续在我心上挖出一小块空间，住了进去。

lines.en: And I continue to hold my breath so I can feel more of her existence.
lines.zh: 而我继续屏住呼吸，好去感受更多关于她的存在。

lines.en: It’s the closest I can ever come to feeling one with her.
lines.zh: 这是我能做到的、与她合为一体最接近的时刻。

{i}Nodoka’s affection has increased to [nodoka_love]!{/i}
lines.zh: {i}Nodoka 的好感度提升到了 [nodoka_love]!{/i}
